t: This is Bayes Business School, the business school of City St George's, University of London. It was established in 1966 and sits just north of the City of London. It takes its name from Thomas Bayes, the eighteenth-century Presbyterian minister and statistician known for Bayes' theorem. The earlier name, Cass, came from Sir John Cass, a merchant, Tory MP and philanthropist who was also a key figure in the Royal African Company, which was involved in the Atlantic slave trade. The two names tell quite different stories.
